title: While Now upon This Sabbath Eve
description: While Now upon This Sabbath Eve in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 97 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Close of Worship. Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: While now up-on this Sab-bath eve, Thy house, Al-might-y God, we leave 'Tis sweet, as sinks the set-ting sun, To think on all our du-ties done.

lines: While now upon this Sabbath eve,
Thy house, Almighty God, we leave
'Tis sweet, as sinks the setting sun,
To think on all our duties done.
Oh! evermore may all our bliss
Be peaceful, pure, divine, like this;
And may each Sabbath, as it flies,
Fit us for joy beyond the skies.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
